items.title: Crossing the Vast Craving: Understanding the Truths, Renouncing the Household, Clearing Eight Distractions

items.zh: 云何了法？謂於苦法能了能觀，於集、滅、道法能了能觀。云何修習於無尋定？謂能了知如是法已，又復安住居家諸欲依持斷滅，及棄出中。
items.en: What is understanding the Dharma? It means being able to understand and observe the truth of suffering, and being able to understand and observe the truths of origination, cessation, and the path. Having thus come to understand these truths, one further comes to abide in the total relinquishment of everything household life depends on, and in going forth from it entirely.

items.zh: 或於阿練若處，或於樹下空閑，
於隨順喜眼所識色所有喜身，於隨順憂眼所識色所有憂身，於隨順捨眼所識色所有捨身，於此所緣無欲尋纏，心多安住；乃至亦無所生家世相應尋纏，心多安住。
items.en: Towards the accumulated pleasure that arises from forms seen by the eye inclining towards delight... regarding these objects, the mind, for the most part, abides free of the entanglement of desirous thought; and so on, up to abiding free even of the entanglement of thoughts bound up with [wealthy, influential] patron households.

items.zh: 設起欲尋，乃至家世相應尋等，即能如實了知出離；不為欲尋之所障礙，乃至不為家世相應尋所障礙，而能靜慮、審慮、諦慮。
由此方便，由此道修，能斷喜身染愛過失，能斷憂身憤恚過失，能斷捨身惛沈過失。諸纏斷故，身得輕安；隨眠斷故，於欲界繫三身染污心善解脫。彼於爾時，名已越度廣大欲愛。
items.en: By this method, by cultivating this path, one is able to sever the fault of craving belonging to pleasure, the fault of hostility belonging to displeasure, and the fault of torpor belonging to neutrality. Because these entanglements are severed, the body attains ease; because their latent tendency is severed, the mind becomes genuinely liberated from the defilement belonging to all three, bound to the sense-desire realm. At this point, one is said to have crossed the vast flood of craving.

items.zh: 謂於諸色乃至諸觸遍流行愛，若和合愛、若增長愛、若不離愛、若不合愛、若退減愛、若別離愛。或於欲界復受生愛。復有差別。云何修習於無尋定？謂已得無尋無伺靜慮。餘如前說。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂彼天女略問世尊三種要義。一者、下分結斷；二者、上分結斷方便；三者、即彼下分結斷方便，及如彼善斷。如是問已，爾時世尊隨應而答。謂由身輕安、心善解脫，答彼所問下分結斷，非斷方便。由無作、繫念、不傾動，答彼所問上分結斷方便，非斷。而於彼斷，天女類前亦即領解。惟餘下分結斷方便，及如彼善斷。爾時世尊先以修無尋定廣說差別，答斷方便。謂若能斷、如斷、所斷。此中了法，說名能斷。修無尋定，說名如斷。所斷憤過，謂瞋恚品；所斷愛過，謂貪欲品；所斷惛沈過，謂愚癡品。如是名為能如所斷。如是廣答斷方便已，唯有所餘如善斷在。復由第二修無尋定差別因緣，答其善斷。

items.title: Topic Four Closes: Thorough Severance, and What the "Waist-Float" Really Is

items.zh: 言善斷者，謂畢竟斷、遠分斷、一切雜染斷。由了知法故，釋畢竟斷；由修無尋定故，釋遠分斷；由貪瞋癡纏及隨眠一切斷故，釋一切雜染斷。
items.en: "Thorough severance" means: final severance, severance at a distance, and severance of all defilement entirely. Final severance is explained by understanding the Dharma; severance at a distance is explained by cultivating concentration free of examination; and severance of all defilement entirely is explained by the complete severing of craving, aversion, and delusion, both their manifestation and their latent tendency.

items.zh: 當知是名此中略義。又彼天女依諸有學未得勝意，已離欲貪，未離上貪，而興請問。
意名腰舟。如經說：慚軸意腰舟。於此腰舟猶未得者，說彼名為未得腰舟。此中何等名為腰舟？謂於諸結善解脫心。
items.en: The mind itself is called the "waist-float." As the sutra says: conscience is the axle, the mind is the waist-float. One who has not yet attained this waist-float is said to lack it. What, here, is meant by the waist-float? A mind genuinely liberated from every fetter.

items.title: Topic Five Opens: A World Never Free of Fear

items.zh: 常有怖世間，眾生恒所厭；於未生眾苦，或復已生中。若有少無怖；今請為我說。
items.en: The world is forever fearful — beings are constantly wearied by it, whether over sufferings not yet arisen, or those already present. If there is even the slightest state free of fear, please, teach it to me now.

items.zh: 天！我觀解脫，不離智精進，不離攝諸根，不離一切捨。
items.en: Deity, as I observe it, liberation is never apart from wisdom and diligence, never apart from restraining the senses, and never apart from relinquishing everything entirely.

items.zh: 我觀極久遠，梵志般涅槃。已過諸恐怖，超世間貪著。今此頌中，始從欲
items.en: As I have observed across a very long time: one who has left desire behind and attained final nirvāṇa has already passed beyond every enmity and fear, transcending the world's own craving entirely.

items.zh: 界乃至有頂諸薩迦耶，皆名世間。此中義者，意在欲界有樂有苦有情世間。

blocks.text: The goddess's questions are answered: how the "vast craving" is crossed and what the "waist-float" is. Then a new deva asks about a world full of fear. A long passage (0373c01–c21) explaining the kinds of craving is untranslated; it is summarised below.

To cross the vast craving, one **understands the Dharma** (the four truths), relinquishes household life, and in solitude clears away **eight kinds of thought**: of desire, ill will, harm, kin, country, immortality, contempt, and households of influence. Master Cháng Bǎi explains the last as cultivating ties with wealthy patrons. Venerable Miào Jìng: "understanding" is a plain grasp; "observing" is deeper investigation.

Through **concentration free of examination** (無尋定), one cuts craving that belongs to pleasure, hostility that belongs to displeasure, and dullness that belongs to neutrality. Master Cháng Bǎi: then one has crossed the vast craving and attained non-return.

The "vast craving" is craving that flows everywhere among forms through touches: craving for union, increase, not parting; craving regarding separation and loss; and craving for rebirth in the desire realm. The verse's three answers correspond to three severances: **final severance** (by understanding the Dharma), **severance at a distance** (by concentration free of examination), and **severance of all defilement** (cutting greed, hatred, and delusion in manifestation and in latent tendency).

"What is the waist-float? A mind genuinely liberated from every fetter." Venerable Miào Jìng: a gourd tied at the waist keeps a swimmer afloat; "waist" stands for the mind, the "float" for calm and insight grounded in non-self. The goddess asked on behalf of trainees who are free of desire-realm craving but not yet of the higher realms.

subs.head: A world never free of fear

blocks.text: A deva says the world is always afraid, and asks how to be free of fear. The Buddha: "Liberation is never apart from wisdom and diligence, never apart from restraining the senses, and never apart from relinquishing everything." Venerable Miào Jìng: without wisdom, however diligent you are, it is in vain.
Master Cháng Bǎi tells of a farmer who lost his harvest and saw that his grief came from clinging to it; seeing that where there is craving there is suffering, he attained stream-entry.

quiz.q: The treatise speaks of being able to "understand and observe" the truth of suffering. How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish the two?
options: understanding is a shallow, clear grasp; observing is deep investigation — they differ in depth
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "being able to understand" is a plain, clear grasp; "observing" is deep investigation — they differ in depth. Having understood the four truths, one abides in relinquishing all that household life depends on and in going forth.

quiz.q: The English renders the last distraction as "thoughts bound up with one's own family status." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain it?
options: thoughts of cultivating ties with wealthy, powerful patrons and frequenting their homes — unrelated to one's own lineage
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi explains the eighth thought, "thoughts bound up with households of influence": cultivating ties with patrons and frequenting wealthy, powerful patrons' homes, stirring up inner mental discourse. The English "one's own family status" differs from the lecture.

quiz.q: By this path, which three faults of the three bodies does the treatise say are severed, and when has one crossed the vast flood of craving?
options: craving of pleasure, hostility of displeasure, torpor of neutrality; entanglement severed gives bodily ease, the latent tendency severed liberates the mind from the three bodies' desire-realm defilement — then the vast craving is crossed
quiz.why: "One is able to sever the fault of craving belonging to pleasure, the fault of hostility belonging to displeasure, and the fault of torpor belonging to neutrality." Master Cháng Bǎi: at that point one is said to have crossed the vast craving — one has now attained non-return.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of "thorough severance," and how does the treatise explain each?
options: final severance by understanding the Dharma; severance at a distance by concentration free of examination; severance of all defilement by severing all entanglement and latent tendency of greed, hatred, and delusion
by seeing, cultivation, and beyond training
quiz.why: "Final severance is explained by understanding the Dharma; severance at a distance is explained by cultivating concentration free of examination; and severance of all defilement entirely is explained by the complete severing of craving, aversion, and delusion, both their manifestation and their latent tendency." Venerable Miào Jìng: concentration free of examination pushes affliction farther and farther away.

quiz.q: The treatise says "the mind is called the waist-float." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the term?
options: a gourd or float tied at the waist for crossing water; he takes "waist" as mind and "float" as non-self calm and insight (precepts, concentration, wisdom), while the treatise defines it as the mind well liberated from all fetters
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: a gourd or other float tied at the waist lets one stay afloat and cross the sea; "waist" stands for the mind, and "float" chiefly for calm and insight grounded in non-self. The treatise: "What, here, is meant by the waist-float? A mind genuinely liberated from every fetter." The readings do not conflict but divide the term differently.

quiz.q: The deity asks whether there is even the slightest state free of fear. How does the Buddha answer?
options: liberation is never apart from wisdom and diligence, from restraining the senses, and from relinquishing everything
quiz.why: "Deity, as I observe it, liberation is never apart from wisdom and diligence, never apart from restraining the senses, and never apart from relinquishing everything entirely." Venerable Miào Jìng: without wisdom, however diligent you are, it is in vain.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi illustrate with the Dharmapada story of the farmer whose rice crop was destroyed by flood?
options: only those with attachment grieve; the farmer realised it was his own attachment to the harvest — where there is craving there is suffering
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: only those with attachment grieve; those without craving are not disturbed by such circumstances. The farmer reflected that it was his own clinging to circumstances — his love of an abundant harvest — because where there is craving there is suffering; and he attained stream-entry.
